summary.title: The Walking Dead - A Survival Guide to Resilient Applications
summary.one_liner: A slide deck introducing fault-tolerant, resilient system design: fault/error/failure terms, availability math, redundancy, error detection, and recovery and mitigation patterns.
takeaways: Faults are latent defects that can cause errors; errors that go uncontained become failures.
Availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR), and 99.999% allows about 5.256 minutes of downtime per year.
Common detection techniques include periodic checks, heartbeats, and routine exercises; recovery includes failover, intelligent retries, restart, and fail fast.
Hystrix is presented as a case study of these patterns in practice.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from a talk by Michael Nitschinger given at Voxxed Days Vienna 2015. It introduces fault tolerance terminology (fault, error, failure), reliability and availability formulas, and a table of downtime per year for different availability levels. It then covers fault-tolerant architecture ideas such as units of mitigation, redundancy costs, escalation, and a fault observer, followed by error detection and recovery patterns. The deck cites external references including Netflix Turbine and Hystrix, and recommends Hanmer's and Nygard's books.
